case.target_concept: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities (CCSS.Math.Content.7.RP.A.2). Students have not yet received direct instruction on this target.
case.subject: mathematics
teacher_recently_taught: Compute unit rates involving fractional quantities (7.RP.A.1).
Add and subtract rational numbers, using numerical and number-line interpretations (7.NS.A.1).

benchmark_context.setting_rule: The generated student task must use a basketball situation involving Stephen Curry. Invented practice or camp data are fictional, not claims about real statistics.
benchmark_context.prior_knowledge_boundary: Treat the two supplied prior standards as the fixed recently taught repertoire. Grounding may unpack these skills, but must not add extra assumed courses, formal proportional-relation methods, variance, fair-division algorithms, or probability instruction.
benchmark_context.task_rule: Generate a new task for exploration before instruction on the target, not a worked example or a lesson teaching the target method.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Compute unit rates involving ratios of fractional quantities, including lengths and areas in like or different units.
Add and subtract rational numbers and interpret these operations numerically and on a number line.

grounding_evidence.label: Unit rates
grounding_evidence.text: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.

grounding_evidence.label: Rational-number addition and subtraction
grounding_evidence.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

misconceptions: Mixes up sides of a ratio
Divides total amount by each side of the ratio instead of dividing by the sum of the parts
Thinks the number in the ratio is the total
Shares equally instead of in given ratio
Thinks a difference of one part in a ratio means the quantities will differ by one unit
In ratio question where one side of ratio is given, treats that as the total

misconception_provenance.selection: Six exact mapping entries retained from the historical eight-label ratio list; two historical labels without an exact mapping match are not asserted to be verbatim Eedi entries.
misconception_provenance.limitation: Documented misconception labels, not student-response frequencies or validated error pathways for these generated tasks.

protocol.sampling_unit: One independent scheduled generation attempt from the common fixed specification; no previous-task memory or seven-brief stratification.
protocol.failure_policy: Thirty attempts per condition, with current bounded within-pipeline repairs. Do not replace blocked, malformed, interrupted, or failed attempts to obtain thirty successes. Missing scores remain missing, not zero.
protocol.rating_policy: One frozen rahimi-table1/v1 Luna rating per ready task, in a seeded shuffled order, with identical assumed learner context, no condition labels, no teacher notes, and no proposed student approaches.
protocol.prior_policy: Fresh mapping and expansion per PIPELINE attempt from the same two official curriculum excerpts. This freezes retrieval to control learner knowledge; it is not an evaluation of retrieval accuracy.
protocol.comparison_scope: Method-package comparison at a shared base model, not equal-compute isolation of one prompt ingredient. Pipeline selection and verification are part of that method; their costs and blocked runs must be reported.
protocol.mathematics_policy: Keep deterministic pipeline checks separate from final-rubric ratings. Direct outputs lack equivalent structured plans and remain not deterministically checked, not invalid. Judge mathematical concerns are unverified model claims.
protocol.paper_setting: Rahimi et al. (2025): Grade 7, 7.RP.A.2, prior 7.RP.A.1 and 7.NS.A.1, sports/basketball/Stephen Curry; thirty completed problems per original model.
departures: Luna in all conditions rather than GPT-4o and Phi-3.
Automated Luna rating rather than two trained independent blinded human raters and third-rater adjudication.
The paper describes but does not reproduce its exact generation prompt or identify its five example texts. Our six-component direct prompt and five literature adaptations are a reconstruction.
The paper's prose mentions six rubric criteria, but its published Table 1 contains five; this benchmark uses the five published dimensions consistently.
The prior standard 7.NS.A.1 specifically covers rational addition/subtraction; the paper's broad phrase 'operations with rational numbers' is not expanded to additional standards.
Thirty scheduled attempts are not a guarantee of thirty completed problems.
V1/V2/V3 retain the historical misconception-input distinction but use a new paper-style shared direct prompt, not the historical modified prompt.
Luna is both generator and evaluator; rubric differences do not establish human agreement, real student approach diversity, or learning.
